evidence.intree_statement: #[export] Program Instance prod_one_l {x : C} : 1 × x ≅ x := { to := exr; from := one △ id }.  (the book's 'true ∧ U = U')
#[export] Program Instance coprod_zero_l {x : C} : 0 + x ≅ x := { to := zero ▽ id; from := inr }.  (the book's 'false ∨ U = U')
#[export] Program Instance exp_zero {x : C} : x^0 ≅ 1 := { to := one; from := curry (zero ∘ to prod_zero_r) }.  (the book's 'false ⇒ U = true')
#[export] Program Instance exp_one {x : C} : x^1 ≅ x := { to := eval ∘ id △ one; from := curry exl }.  (the book's 'true ⇒ U = U')
#[export] Program Instance one_exp {x : C} : 1^x ≅ 1 := { to := one; from := curry one }.  (the book's 'U ⇒ true = true')
#[export] Program Instance prod_zero_l {x : C} : 0 × x ≅ 0 := { to := uncurry zero; from := zero }.  (the book's 'false ∧ U = false')

statement_record.book: In the Heyting algebra of opens of a space: the open acting as 'true' is X (X ∧ U = U, X ∨ U = X, U ⇒ X = X, X ⇒ U = U) and the open acting as 'false' is ∅ (∅ ∨ U = U, ∅ ∧ U = ∅, ∅ ⇒ U = X).
statement_record.intree: In any bicartesian closed category the corresponding unit/annihilator isomorphisms are proved: 1 × x ≅ x, 0 + x ≅ x, 0 × x ≅ 0, x^0 ≅ 1, x^1 ≅ x, 1^x ≅ 1 (indexed as high-school algebra in Theory/Algebra.v:68-88).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on two counts: (a) six of the exercise's seven clauses are proved only for a general BiCCC, never for opens of a space (no topological space or frame exists in-tree); (b) the seventh clause, 'true ∨ U = true' (1 + x ≅ 1), is FALSE in a general bicartesian closed category and is a genuinely posetal/lattice fact — the library has no lemma for it and no notion of thin/posetal category on which to state it. Conversely the in-tree isomorphisms are ≅ (invertible morphisms) rather than the equalities a poset gives, which is the faithful setoid rephrasing.

gap: Two gaps. (1) No topological space and no poset of opens, so 'true = X' and 'false = ∅' cannot be stated; the in-tree laws are about a generic terminal 1 and initial 0. (2) The clause 'true ∨ U = true' (i.e. 1 + x ≅ 1) is absent and is not derivable in the generic bicartesian closed setting the other six clauses live in — it needs posetality, which the library does not axiomatise (Instance/Props.v gives one thin bicartesian closed model but proves no such absorption law).
